title: Suresh Pal v. State of Uttar Pradesh

facts: The victim was stabbed during a quarrel and before dying gave a statement to the Magistrate naming the accused.
A case of murder under Section 302 IPC was registered against the accused and his brother <CITATION>.
issues: Whether the dying declaration under Section 32 of the Evidence Act and the joint attack establish murder with common intention.
arguments: Learned counsel for the accused submitted that the declaration was tutored.
reasoning: As held in Ramesh Kumar v. State of Rajasthan, AIR 1985 SC 1461, common intention may develop on the spot.

facts: The young wife was found dead of burns two years after marriage and her father alleged dowry harassment.
The police also produced an alleged confession of the husband recorded by the investigating officer.
issues: Whether the dowry death presumption applies and whether the confession to police can be relied upon.
arguments: It was contended for the husband that the death was suicide.
reasoning: The confession is excluded by Section 25 of the Evidence Act, see (1994) 3 SCC 112.
decision: The conviction under Section 304B IPC is upheld on other evidence.

facts: The buyer issued a post-dated cheque for goods supplied under a written agreement and the cheque bounced.
The seller filed a complaint under Section 138 N.I. Act after sending notice.
issues: Whether the cheque was for an enforceable debt arising from a concluded contract.
arguments: Learned counsel for the accused submitted that the supply was defective.
reasoning: The presumption under the Act was not rebutted.

title: Orbit Finance v. Gupta Polymers Ltd.

facts: A cheque issued by a private company bounced and the complainant arrayed every director as an accused.
The complaint was filed under Sections 138 and 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.
issues: Whether directors can be prosecuted without averments that they were in charge of the business.
arguments: It was contended that the directors were independent directors.
decision: The proceedings are quashed against two directors.

title: Ravi Shankar v. State of Bihar

facts: The wife had complained of cruelty by her husband and was last seen with him before her body was found.
There was no eye witness and the husband was charged with murder under Section 302 and cruelty under Section 498A IPC.
issues: Whether the circumstantial evidence, including the last seen circumstance, proves murder beyond reasonable doubt.
arguments: Learned counsel for the husband submitted that the chain of circumstances is incomplete.

title: Deputy Commissioner v. Harbour Link Pvt. Ltd.

facts: The assessee built a container terminal at a port under a concession agreement and claimed deduction under Section 80-IA of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
The Assessing Officer held that the terminal was not an infrastructure facility.
issues: Whether a container terminal at a port is an infrastructure facility eligible for the 80IA deduction.
arguments: It was contended by the Revenue that the assessee was only a contractor.
decision: The appeal of the Revenue is dismissed.
